correctness.rationale: The nine-edge graph, six matrices and 10-state transitions define a complete finite integer proof. Each of six payoff tables passes min(R,P)>max(S,T); four BR moves strictly increase utility, six I moves copy a unique highest-payoff neighbor, and all ten effective transitions close a cycle. The sixth vertex is idle at the cycle start, permitting an 11-activation uniformly persistent schedule. An independent implementation of the exact update equations in verify_cycle.py rechecks every computation and three schedule periods. There is no numerical extrapolation, hidden parameter range, normalization or infinitary assumption.

originality.rationale: The originating 2023 paper explicitly asks whether non-equilibration occurs under some persistent activation sequence in arbitrary mixed imitation/BR opponent-coordinating networks, while its convergence theorems cover paths, cycles, stars and sparse trees. Its formal Eq. (2) is neighbor-only payoff-maximizing imitation. The six-agent connected graph with triangles and its ten-switch exact fair orbit are outside the earlier classes and answer the existential question. The 2022 Sakhaei–Maleki–Ramazi almost-sure equilibration theorem does not imply equilibration for all deterministic fair schedules; the 2022 pure-imitation theorem excludes BR nodes. No searched record establishes this particular construction or a dominating general theorem. Unindexed and more recent equivalent examples cannot be ruled out.

value.rationale: The motivating primary source explicitly identifies existence of nonconvergent mixed dynamics on arbitrary networks as an open structural question. An explicit connected counterexample with strict opponent coordination and a genuinely fair schedule closes this existential gap, forbids the proposed universal strict potential, and separates deterministic every-schedule convergence from almost-sure results. It uses small integer data and a fully auditable orbit, not an arbitrary invariant or an incremental numerical bound.
